For the HPC team: the session stays protected by its password, as they require. What changes is who types it: for the web UI the dashboard posts it, from the card only the session's owner can see. The app also refuses requests that the proxy marks as another user's (X-Forwarded-User).

docs.title: First release of this layout (3.0.0)
docs.text:
Versions before 3.0.0 have the path of their code ($TEXT_LAB_BASE/src_main280526/src) in the deployed launch script and read no site configuration. Version 3.0.0 is the first to read site.env and serve current, so the switch needs the HPC team once:

  1. Prepare the shared folder without touching the running deployment: the release folder releases/v3.0.0, current pointing to it, and site.env. The old launch script reads none of them.
  2. Rehearse in a sandbox app without dev.env: it then runs exactly what production will run.
  3. Ask the HPC team to deploy the Open OnDemand files from tag v3.0.0. Merge to main close to that date, since merging publishes the new user guide.
  4. Start a session on the production app and check output.log and each feature.
  5. To roll back, the HPC team redeploys the files of v2.2.1, which still serve src_main280526; keep that folder until 3.0.0 has run without problems for a while.
  6. Afterwards, remove src_main280526 and the old versions' session logs (logs/). ollama_tmp/ and run_olmocr.sh in the shared folder are used by no version in the repository; check with their owners before removing them.

docs.title: Where tests live
docs.text:
• Feature tests live next to their feature, in src/textlab/features/<feature>/tests/.
  • Cross-cutting tests live in tests/: checks that no user data is written outside the job workspace and that no site-specific values are hardcoded (test_data_footprint.py), that the site configuration provides every setting (test_site_config.py), and that the launcher and the Open OnDemand files start the interface TEXT_LAB_UI names (test_launch.py).
  • Web UI tests live in src/textlab/ui/web/tests/. They call the routes with FastAPI's test client, logged in or not: login, CSRF tokens, every page, jobs from submission to download (with a demo job that needs no model and only the tests serve, demo_job.py), uploads, and rules for the templates and static files (no inline scripts or styles, every icon vendored).

Shared code has its tests in src/textlab/common/tests/. Each tests/ folder is a package (it has an __init__.py), so a test can import helpers from another test module by its full name, for example from textlab.features.translation.tests.test_translation_pdf import make_pdf.

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
Tests that need more than plain Python are marked, so they can be selected or skipped:

Marker Meaning gpu Needs a CUDA GPU container Needs the Text Lab image (models, binaries such as Tesseract) ollama Needs a running Ollama server slow Takes more than about a minute

Unregistered markers are an error (--strict-markers), so add new ones to pyproject.toml first.

Most tests replace models and servers with fakes, so they run anywhere: for example features/transcription/tests/test_service.py fakes WhisperX and ffmpeg, and common/tests/test_ollama.py fakes the Ollama client. A few tests run the real thing and carry the container marker, such as features/transcription/tests/test_integration.py; they skip themselves when the model stores are not mounted. Tests of worker processes start real subprocesses with a stub worker (common/tests/stub_worker.py). The PaddleOCR-VL and PaddleOCR workers are tested the same way: features/ocr/tests/ writes stub scripts that speak their protocol and passes them as worker_path.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text: The tests run inside the Apptainer image on a compute node, never on a login node. scripts/test_on_node.sbatch wraps the command.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
The image does not include pytest. Install it once into your home directory, from a compute node:

SIF=/storage/research/dsl_shared/solutions/ondemand/text_lab/container/text_lab_210526.sif
apptainer exec --env PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 "$SIF" \
  /opt/conda/envs/text_lab_main/bin/python -m pip install \
  --target "$HOME/.cache/text_lab_pytest" pytest

Warnings from pip's dependency resolver during this install are harmless.

docs.title: As a batch job
docs.text:
From the repository root:

sbatch --qos=job_gratis scripts/test_on_node.sbatch
sbatch --qos=job_gratis scripts/test_on_node.sbatch -m "not slow"

The output goes to textlab-tests-<jobid>.out in the repository root. Arguments after the script name are passed to pytest.

docs.title: In an interactive session
docs.text:
From an srun or salloc session on a compute node:

bash scripts/test_on_node.sbatch -k translation

The script refuses to run outside a Slurm allocation. It reads the site configuration (deploy/site.env in the repository, or TEXT_LAB_SITE_ENV) for the image and the model stores, and mounts them as the app does, so the container tests find the models. TL_CONTAINER selects a different image, for example a newly built one.

docs.title: Lint and architecture checks
docs.text:
These are lightweight and also run on GitHub for every push:

ruff check .            # PEP 8, docstrings, import order, likely bugs
ruff format --check .   # formatting
lint-imports            # backend never imports a user interface

lint-imports needs src on the Python path (PYTHONPATH=src). Code not refactored yet is excluded from ruff (extend-exclude in pyproject.toml); refactoring a module removes it from that list.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request:

  • ruff lint and format checks
  • a syntax check of all Python files
  • the import-linter contracts
  • a strict build of this documentation site

GitHub's machines have no GPU and no image, so the tests do not run there: run them on a compute node and give the Slurm job ID in the pull request.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text: main is protected: changes arrive through pull requests, and a pull request can be merged only when both CI jobs pass. The pull request template (.github/pull_request_template.md) asks for what CI cannot check: the test job ID, a UI check in a sandbox app, updated documentation, no emojis, and an explanation of any change to model-facing prompts.

docs.title: Web UI migration plan
docs.text:
Status

Plan agreed on 26 November 2026; phase 0 done the same day (see Phase 0 results). Phase 1 built the foundation, the launcher and the redeployment files, and the mockups of Home and Transcription were agreed on 27 November (see Phase 1 progress). Phase 2, the pilot, was tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November (see Phase 2 progress). Phase 3 started with Meeting Notes; every page followed, each tried in the sandbox and committed, the last, Knowledge Graph, on 27 November, followed by a clean-up (see Phase 3 progress). Next is phase 4, the switch. The work happens on the local branch feat/web-ui, one commit per phase or page, and reaches main when the whole UI is done. Update this page when a phase ends or a decision changes.

Text Lab's user interface moves from Streamlit to a web UI built with FastAPI, Jinja2 templates and HTMX, with a fresh, modern and responsive design. The backend (features/, common/) stays as it is: since version 3.0.0 every page calls only its feature's service.py, and the new pages do the same.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• Long runs tie up the page. A Streamlit page runs a transcription or an OCR batch inside the page script: the tab has to stay open until the run ends, and reloading the page loses its result.
  • Two runs can break each other. Starting a feature releases the GPU for it (gpu_manager.prepare_gpu), which stops the GPU workers of other features, including a run still going in another browser tab.
  • Every click reruns the page script, which makes pages slow and their state fragile (session-state keys, st.rerun).
  • The look is Streamlit's. Layout, components and behaviour on small screens can hardly be changed beyond what Streamlit offers.
  • Pages cannot be tested. Tests can only read the page sources; the routes of a web app can be called and checked with FastAPI's test client.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
Question Decision Reason How users switch At once, when every page exists in the new UI. Streamlit stays selectable for one release as a rollback, then it is removed A fresh design next to Streamlit pages would feel like two apps, and keeping two UIs doubles every UI change How it is built Page by page on one local branch (feat/web-ui), committed per phase or page, merged into main once every page exists; then one release and one HPC redeploy One developer, no reviewers to wait for; production is stable and main sees no changes meanwhile (should a fix land on main, merge it into the branch) Design Fresh: modern, responsive, easy to use, accessible Long runs Background jobs, one GPU job at a time, results kept for the session Users can leave or reload a page, and runs can no longer take the GPU from each other First pages Home and Transcription Transcription has the cleanest service: a worker process, progress reports and cancelling

Considered and rejected:

  • Both UIs in one server. Streamlit 1.61's st.App can mount other routes, so FastAPI pages could replace Streamlit pages one at a time. That only helps a page-by-page switch, which mixes two designs.
  • Streamlit as a permanent second option: two UIs to keep working for every change.

During the migration the Streamlit pages get bug fixes only. New behaviour goes into the services, where both UIs use it, or into the new pages.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
src/textlab/ui/
├── launch.py          # starts the UI that TEXT_LAB_UI names
├── streamlit/         # the current UI, removed after the switch
└── web/
    ├── app.py         # app factory: routes, middleware, static files
    ├── auth.py        # login with the session password, cookie, CSRF
    ├── jobs.py        # job queue, progress, cancelling, SSE
    ├── uploads.py     # streams uploads into the job workspace
    ├── render.py      # templates, icons, links from the base path
    ├── settings.py    # the server's settings
    ├── server.py      # uvicorn, started by the launcher
    ├── pages/         # one module per page: its routes; the navigation
    ├── templates/     # Jinja2: base layout, components, one folder per page
    ├── static/
    │   ├── css/       # design system: tokens, layout, components
    │   ├── js/        # app.js (live updates, forms), theme.js
    │   └── vendor/    # htmx, icons, later plotly.js (pinned)
    ├── tests/
    └── README.md      # how a page is built

docs.title: How a page works
docs.text:
1. GET /transcription returns the whole page: the base layout (navigation, header, job indicator) around the page's template.
  2. The form is sent with HTMX (hx-post, multipart). The route checks the options, streams the upload into the workspace, submits a job and returns a job card for the page's result area.
  3. The page follows its jobs over server-sent events (SSE), in one stream for all of them (/events?page=<id>; phase 0 shows why). static/js/app.js opens it while one of the session's jobs waits or runs, and closes it when the server says that none does. Each event carries the changed job cards and the job indicator as out-of-band fragments; the card of a finished job holds its result.
  4. Downloads are plain links (/jobs/<id>/files/<name>).

Rules, checked by tests as for the Streamlit pages today:

  • A page module imports only the features' service modules, and uses only the names they export in __all__. What a page needs beyond that goes into the service.
  • No processing in routes or templates.
  • No inline scripts: JavaScript lives in files under static/.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
• uvicorn with one worker process: logins, jobs and results live in memory, and each Open OnDemand session has one user.
  • Routes that call services are plain def functions, which FastAPI runs in a thread pool. The heavy work already runs in worker processes or in Ollama.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• A design system in plain CSS, typographic rather than boxy: ink on paper, structure from rules and a grid instead of cards and shadows, the red of the Text Lab logo as the one accent. IBM Plex Sans carries the text (condensed for titles) and IBM Plex Mono the labels, numbers, times and file names; both are vendored (SIL Open Font License), so no fonts are loaded from elsewhere. Custom properties for colours, type, spacing; light and dark themes that follow the system setting, with a switch. The first draft used system fonts and rounded cards, and looked like every other web app; the second (27 November 2026) gave the UI a character of its own.
  • Responsive layout: the navigation is a numbered index of the tools, grouped by what they work on (audio, documents, text, data), on the left on wide screens and behind a menu button on narrow ones. A status bar on top shows when the session ends (Slurm's SLURM_JOB_END_TIME), the jobs, the theme and signing out. Text keeps a readable width; pages work from a phone to a wide monitor.
  • Shared components: page masthead, forms as sheets of numbered steps, file drop zone (drag and drop, the chosen files with their sizes), options with their explanations, job records with status and progress (current step, elapsed time, cancel), result tabs, file listings for downloads, notices (information, warning, error with details for support), "Models used" lists, job indicator.
  • Icons: few, from a vendored open-source SVG set (Lucide, ISC licence), for arrows, downloads, playing and closing. No emojis.
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, everything usable with the keyboard, visible focus, labelled fields, progress announced to screen readers, reduced motion respected.
  • No build step and no CDN. htmx 2.0.11 (the current release on npm, where htmx 4 is tagged next, not latest), the Lucide icons (1.71.0, only those used), the IBM Plex fonts (5.3.0) and later plotly.js are vendored in static/vendor/. Each is pinned and checked against the registry's checksum, with its version, source and licence in static/vendor/README.md. Browsers fetch nothing from outside the cluster. htmx's SSE extension is not used: the page's one stream opens and closes with the session's active jobs, which a few lines of app.js handle.
  • Mockups first. Static mockups of Home and Transcription are agreed before the pilot pages are built.

docs.title: Jobs and the GPU
docs.text:
• A job is one run: a recording or a ZIP batch to transcribe, a document or a batch to read, a topic model to fit. A page submits it and shows its progress; the user can leave the page or reload it and find the result again.
  • One GPU job at a time. Further jobs wait in order, and their card says so ("waiting, 1 job ahead"). The runner calls gpu_manager.prepare_gpu(<feature>) when a job starts, not when it is submitted, so a waiting job never stops a running one.
  • Short GPU requests (a chat message, the translation editor, a meeting summary) also wait for a running job; the page says which job is running and offers to cancel it. If this proves too strict, measure whether a small LLM fits on the GPU next to a running job. The translation editor and Chat run each request as a job that is not listed (listed=False) and show it in place (their own card_template): a request held open while a model loads could pass the proxy's timeout, and a job reports progress and can be stopped.
  • Progress comes from the services' on_progress callbacks and reaches the page over SSE, in the page's one event stream, which is open only while one of its jobs runs or waits. After a reload, the page reconnects to its jobs.
  • Cancelling: a waiting job is removed; a running one gets its service's cancel event. Only Transcription and Topic Modeling take cancel today; the other services get it when their page is built (common.jobs.run_worker already stops workers).
  • Results stay in memory in the job, as they stay in Streamlit's session state today, until the user removes them or the session ends. Uploads are staged in the workspace and removed when the job ends, so the privacy promises of the user guide stay true.
  • The job indicator in the header lists running and waiting jobs and recent results, on every page.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Login with the session password shown on the Open OnDemand dashboard (TOKEN), compared in constant time, then a signed session cookie (itsdangerous): HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, limited to the session's path (/node/<host>/<port>/).
  • The user named by the proxy (X-Forwarded-User) is checked too: a request naming another user is refused. The header cannot replace the password: the server listens on the node's network so that the proxy reaches it, and a direct connection can send any header.
  • Connect without copying the password (decided in phase 1): for the web UI, the dashboard's Connect button posts the password to the login route; only the session's owner sees the card that holds it. The card needs to know the interface, which before.sh.erb reads from the configuration (template/config.sh) and passes as text_lab_ui (conn_params). Streamlit sessions show the password to copy, as now. A login posted from another origin than the portal is refused.
  • A CSRF token on every request that changes something (HTMX sends it as a header). All Open OnDemand apps share one origin, so the browser alone does not keep other pages from sending requests to Text Lab.
  • A Content Security Policy: scripts only from the app's static files, no inline scripts, htmx's eval turned off.
  • Uploads: a size limit (10 GB, as now), safe file names (common.upload_safety), streamed to the workspace, never held in memory whole.
  • Output: templates escape everything; text from models (Markdown, HTML) is shown as text or sanitized (common.html_safety).

docs.title: Deployment and the switch
docs.text:
• One HPC redeploy, at the switch. template/script.sh.erb starts python -m textlab.ui.launch instead of Streamlit. The launcher starts the UI that TEXT_LAB_UI names (streamlit by default, or web), with today's port, base path and upload limit, so production behaves as before, and names its log (streamlit.log or textlab.log). For releases without the launcher the script starts Streamlit directly, so rollbacks keep working. The Connect change goes into the same redeploy; Deployment lists the files and the order.
  • Sandbox: TEXT_LAB_UI=web in template/dev.env shows the new UI.
  • The switch: the release with the whole UI, the HPC redeploy of its Open OnDemand files, then TEXT_LAB_UI=web in the live site.env. Rolling back means setting it back, without another redeploy.
  • Removal: one release later, the launcher starts only the web UI, and Streamlit leaves the image at its next rebuild (locks/main.txt and text_lab.def).

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: Phase Content Done when 0. Spike (done) A minimal FastAPI app in the sandbox, behind the Open OnDemand proxy: base path, login cookie, SSE progress, a 2 GB upload streamed to the workspace, a download All of it works, or a fallback is chosen (HTMX polling every second instead of SSE) 1. Foundation (done) The launcher and the redeployment files (deployed at the switch). In ui/web/: app factory, login, CSRF, CSP, layout, design system and components, job runner (queue, SSE, cancelling), upload and download helpers, error pages, test harness. Mockups of Home and Transcription An empty app with login, navigation and a demo job runs in the sandbox, with tests, and the mockups are agreed 2. Pilot (done) Home and Transcription: a recording or a ZIP batch, language and model, voice activity detection, speaker identification with speaker counts, the audio player with word highlighting, every download Everything the Streamlit page does works, with tests, and the UI test passes 3. Pages (done) One commit each, in this order: Meeting Notes, Translation, OCR (one page with a switcher, one commit per tool: Standard (the automatic pipeline), Choose an engine (the legacy engines), then historic handwriting and Hugging Face models together; survey extraction left out), Topic Modeling, Chat, Visualize Data, Knowledge Graph As in phase 2, with the page's user guide drafted 4. Switch The branch merged into main; the new user guide replaces the old one; a release, the HPC redeploy, TEXT_LAB_UI=web in production Users work in the new UI; Streamlit can still be selected as a rollback 5. Removal ui/streamlit/ and its tests are removed; Streamlit leaves the image One release after the switch, without a rollback

docs.title: What is rebuilt
docs.text:
The Streamlit code to replace, about 8,400 lines in all:

Page Lines Notes Home 120 Transcription 900 with the audio player Meeting Notes 1,270 transcribes first, then summarizes with citations Translation 900 text editor with a model kept loaded, documents OCR 2,310 automatic mode, results, review, legacy engines, historic handwriting, Hugging Face models Topic Modeling 1,060 charts, editable tables Chat 520 streamed answers, documents, charts Visualize Data 420 analysis in the background, charts Knowledge Graph 710 Grobid, graph view Shared 200 login, disclaimer, GPU notices, progress box

docs.title: Phase 0 results
docs.text:
On 26 November 2026 the spike (scripts/web_ui_spike/, kept until phase 1 replaces it) ran in a Slurm job on a GPU node and was tested in Chrome through the Open OnDemand proxy. Everything the plan depends on works; one finding changes the design.

Check Result Base path Pages, scripts and style sheets work under /node/<host>/<port>/, with the app mounted under that path and every link built from it Login The session cookie works behind the proxy with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict and the session's path, and scripts cannot read it. A plain form posts through the proxy, so Connect can post the password too CSRF and CSP Requests without the token are refused. The strict Content Security Policy causes no violations with htmx 2.0.11 (includeIndicatorStyles and allowEval off) Live progress The proxy does not buffer server-sent events: 40 events in 20 seconds arrived on time (spread 0.05 s). With keep-alive comments every 15 seconds, streams lasted over 3 minutes through 50-second gaps without reconnecting. A job reattached after a page reload. Polling works as well Closed pages The server notices a closed page at its next write to the stream, within 15 seconds with the keep-alive comments, so no stream is left open Uploads 100 MB, 1,100 MB and 2,200 MB passed the proxy at 50 to 120 MB/s, so no limit applies up to at least 2.2 GB. The server's memory stayed at about 80 MB: uploads go to disk Downloads A streamed 1,100 MB download arrived complete (68 MB/s); a file name with umlauts was saved correctly

The proxy forwards the backend's own host and scheme (Host: gnode35.hpc.unibe.ch:47983, http), with the original ones in X-Forwarded-Host (ondemand.hpc.unibe.ch) and X-Forwarded-Proto (https), and the logged-in user in X-Forwarded-User.

Consequences, already worked into the sections above:

  • The browser speaks HTTP/1.1 to the proxy, so it opens at most 6 connections to ondemand.hpc.unibe.ch at a time, for all its tabs on the site together, other Open OnDemand apps included. An open event stream holds one for as long as it is open. In the spike, three streams, two uploads and a download held all six, and polling requests waited: the 10-second polling job made 8 requests, against 11 when it ran alone. Nothing failed. So each page has one event stream for all its jobs and the job indicator, open only while a job runs or waits, and uploads run one at a time.
  • Links are built from the base path, never from the request's host and scheme, which are the backend's.
  • X-Forwarded-User is an extra check, not a replacement for the password (see Security).
  • Uploads are spooled to TMPDIR, which the launch script already places in the private workspace, then copied to their job's folder (1.6 seconds for 2.2 GB).

docs.title: Phase 1 progress
docs.text:
Built on 26 November 2026, with tests (src/textlab/ui/web/tests/, tests/test_launch.py):

  • The launcher and the redeployment files (see Deployment).
  • The app factory under the base path, with the Content Security Policy, the check of X-Forwarded-User and the upload limit (also for uploads that do not announce their size).
  • Login with the session password (Connect posts it), the session cookie, CSRF tokens; every route but the login requires a session.
  • The layout (the index of tools, the status bar with the session's end, the job indicator and the theme switch, the footer with the disclaimer), the design system and the shared components; light and dark; narrow and wide screens. The design was redone on 27 November after the first review (see Design).
  • The job runner: a queue, one job at a time, prepare_gpu at the start, cancelling, progress, results and downloads; short GPU requests (exclusive()); the event stream and the job cards.
  • Error pages and notices, with an error id for unexpected errors.
  • Developer pages under /dev: the component gallery, the mockups of Home and Transcription, and a demo job. Removed before the switch (see Clean-up before the switch).

The mockups were agreed on 27 November, with their choices: the language is detected in the job, from the recording's first 30 seconds, instead of when the file is chosen (the web page uploads the file only when the job is submitted); the result shows the player and the transcript together, with the plain text and the models in tabs; every output file downloads on its own, besides the ZIP of all of them. The mockups were removed when the pages were built.

Still to do from phase 1, with phase 2's sandbox test: try the foundation with TEXT_LAB_UI=web (login through Connect, the demo job, cancelling, a reload while a job runs, narrow screens) and without it (Streamlit as before). The spike (scripts/web_ui_spike/) is removed. The release and the HPC redeployment wait for the switch (phase 4).

docs.title: Phase 2 progress
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, with tests (src/textlab/ui/web/tests/test_transcription_page.py, and in features/transcription/tests/ for the service's new parts):

  • Home (pages/home.py): what Text Lab is, the tools, the session's jobs (updated live from the page's event stream) and where to get help. A notice said which tools were not built yet, until every tool was.
  • Transcription (pages/transcription.py), with the three uses of the Streamlit page:
    • One recording: a job that prepares the recording for the browser (an MP3 and its waveform, service.prepare_playback), transcribes it and offers every export, and a ZIP of all of them with a WAV copy for ELAN, as before.
    • A ZIP of recordings: checked when it arrives (it must hold recordings), transcribed with the same settings, one ZIP with a folder per recording; skipped recordings are listed.
    • Review a transcript: a recording and a transcript table, uploaded or named by their paths on the cluster. It needs no GPU, so it runs beside the queue (JobRunner.submit(..., at_once=True)) and does not wait for a running transcription.
  • The player, in app.js: the browser's own <audio> element plays the MP3 from the job's files (with range requests, so long recordings start at once and seeking works); the waveform is drawn from levels measured on the server. The passage and the word being spoken are marked, the transcript follows, clicking a time, a word or the waveform plays from there, and the waveform works as a slider from the keyboard. Unlike the Streamlit player, it plays the whole recording, not the first 30 minutes.
  • The service (features/transcription/service.py) exports what pages use in __all__, with new helpers: the passages for a player (turns, turns_from_table), the recording for the browser (prepare_playback), the exports on disk (save_transcript_files, save_zip), the recordings in a ZIP (zip_recordings) and language names. The rules test now also checks names read as service.x.
  • The user guide's draft: docs/next/transcription.md, left out of the published site (exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml).

A test runs a recording through the page with the real pipeline (Whisper "tiny" on a generated tone, in the image, marked container and slow): the worker, ffmpeg, the MP3 and the ZIP with its WAV work together. The sandbox test passed on 27 November, and phase 2 was committed.

docs.title: Meeting Notes
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, with tests (src/textlab/ui/web/tests/test_meeting_notes_page.py, and in features/meeting_notes/tests/ for summarize):

  • From a recording: one job transcribes the recording (with the Transcription page's settings: language, speaker counts), then releases the GPU for the language model (JobContext.use_gpu) and summarizes. The transcription has the whole GPU: the job's language model is loaded only for the second step. From a transcript: a segment table, a text file or pasted text; the job names its model (ollama_model), so the GPU release keeps it loaded.
  • While it runs, the card shows the summary as the model writes it (JobContext.preview, at most once a second). Cancelling stops the model between tokens.
  • The result: the summary rendered from Markdown on the server (render.markdown: raw HTML escaped, no images, links in a new tab), with its citations as the passages' times. With a recording, the player's controls sit above the tabs and every citation plays its passage; without one, a citation shows its line in the Transcript tab. Sources, the transcript (with the player, as on Transcription), and the downloads of the Streamlit page.
  • Speakers are named Speaker 1, Speaker 2 by order of appearance, as on Transcription, in the summary, its sources and the transcript. Summarize again (below a result) gives them names and chooses another type, model or language: a new job from the same transcript, with the recording linked into it, no new transcription. The Streamlit page's "Clear GPU memory" is gone: jobs release the GPU themselves.
  • A failed summary keeps the transcript as the result, with the error and the form to summarize again open, as the Streamlit page's retry did.
  • summarize() in the meeting notes service does the single-pass or chunked summary in one call, with progress, the text so far and cancelling; summary_models() and server_ready() also moved out of the page. The player became macros shared by both pages (templates/components/player.html).
  • The user guide's draft: docs/next/meeting_notes.md.
  • Fixed with it: the Menu button showed on wide screens, where the index is always visible, so it did nothing there; it now shows only on narrow screens, where it opens the index (a test checks the rule order).
  • markdown-it-py is named in text_lab.def (it was in the lock already, through rich), so it stays if rich goes; no rebuild is needed.

Fixed after the first sandbox run: the form's language model field was called model, which the Transcription page's settings (reused here) read as another Whisper model, so the transcription tried to load the language model. The field is now llm, Meeting Notes reads the transcription settings without another model (read_options(form, other_model=False)), and a test checks it.

Still to do: try Meeting Notes in the sandbox against the Streamlit page (both sources, each summary type, a long recording that is summarized in chunks, citations that play, summarizing again with names, a failure such as a model that is not installed, cancelling while it writes). Committed on 27 November (b165b39).

docs.title: Translation
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, with tests (src/textlab/ui/web/tests/test_translation_page.py, with faked models and the real service, and in features/translation/tests/ for the service's new parts). The Streamlit page's look and its limits were one of the reasons for the new UI, so the page was designed anew rather than ported:

  • One form for both uses: the languages (From, a swap button, To) and two settings shared by text and documents, folded to one line each (Engine with each engine's description, the model and formality for a language model; Glossary as rows of term and translation). The switcher shows the editor or the documents' steps.
  • The editor: the text on the left, the translation on the right. There is no Load model step any more: the first translation with an engine loads it and says so. Each translation is a job that is not listed (see Jobs and the GPU); a short one comes back with the answer to the request (the route waits up to 1.5 s), a longer one follows over the event stream, with the previous translation dimmed until the new one is ready. A new translation stops and drops the one before. Stop cancels; a translation that waits names the job it waits for and offers to cancel it. Detect language is the default source: it is detected in the job, and the menu then names it. Ctrl + Enter translates, Translate as I type translates after a pause (the choice is remembered in the browser), the swap button translates the translation back, Copy copies it. Up to 20,000 characters (longer texts go through Documents as .txt). The page keeps the text and the settings in memory for the session, so a reload shows them again.
  • Documents: files and ZIP archives, translated by a job with cancelling. With Detect language, each document's language is detected; with a chosen language, that one is used (the Streamlit page's separate check box is gone). The result lists each document with its language, its files, the PDF checks, and Compare source and translation: the passages side by side in the page (the first 300; the side-by-side file has all). With several files, the record's listing offers the ZIP of all; with one, the file itself.
  • The service (features/translation/service.py): cancel for translate_text and translate_documents (the document code now lets CancelledError through where it ignored progress errors or blocked an output), each document's pairs in DocumentResults.pairs, documents without a source language detected or reported, and languages, language_name, ollama_models, server_ready, SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS, PDF_OUTPUTS for pages. The engine table gives each backend a short name and a description; the Streamlit page's labels are unchanged.
  • The job runner: listed=False jobs stay out of the job indicator and Home; card_template gives a job its own card; card templates also get the running job.
  • Two Lucide icons added (arrow-left-right, copy), from the same release.
  • The user guide's draft: docs/next/translate.md.

Still to do: try Translation in the sandbox against the Streamlit page (a text with each engine, detection, the glossary, swapping, translating as you type, a long text that follows over the event stream, a translation while a transcription runs, Stop; documents of each type, a ZIP, a mixed batch with detection, PDFs with each output and LaTeX, cancelling, a PDF whose output is blocked; narrow screens and the dark theme), then commit it. The sandbox test passed on 27 November.

docs.title: OCR
docs.text:
One page with a switcher for the four tools (decided on 27 November), one commit per tool. Survey extraction is left out (see Open questions).

Standard (the automatic pipeline; first called Automatic, renamed after the first review), built on 27 November 2026, with tests (src/textlab/ui/web/tests/test_ocr_page.py, with the pipeline faked and the rest of the service real, and in features/ocr/tests/):

  • One drop zone for a PDF, an image or a ZIP; a ZIP is read as a batch (the Streamlit page's two workflows become one). Options: searchable PDF (on by default, also for batches) with the language for placing words, highest quality, describe figures. The survey options are gone.
  • The result shows each page beside its text: the regions outlined on the page image (an SVG of <rect>s, coloured by type, with a legend), and the page's text block by block in reading order, each labelled with its type in the same colour. Pointing at an outline or a block marks both; clicking an outline brings its text into view. Pages one at a time, with a page choice and arrows. Tabs for the tables (each with its CSV), the figures (with generated descriptions apart from the printed caption), and the models used, for citation. Check boxes as read (filled, empty, uncertain), with a notice of uncertain marks. Every download in the record's file listing, Everything first.
  • A batch gives the ZIP of the Streamlit page and an overview of its files: pages, how many from the text layer, what was found, time.
  • The service (features/ocr/service.py): cancel for recognize_document and recognize_batch (the pipeline checks between pages and files; the PaddleOCR-VL worker, resident or one-shot, is killed at once), BatchResult.files, and save_document, which writes a result's downloads, page images, figures and table CSVs into the job's outputs and returns the pages, regions (boxes, sanitized table HTML, LaTeX, figure files, descriptions, marks), tables, figures and models to show. The page keeps only that, not the document with its images.
  • Region colours as tokens (--region-*, from the existing hues, so they follow the theme); the Lucide arrow-left icon added.
  • The user guide's draft: docs/next/ocr.md.
  • Fixed after the first sandbox run: a ZIP batch took 16 minutes, because the resident PaddleOCR-VL worker stalled on its first file until the stall limit (900 s) stopped it; the one-shot fallback then read the five pages in 43 s. The worker inherited the session's OMP_NUM_THREADS=16: the Streamlit OCR page had set it to 1 for its whole process, which the web UI does not do, and the workers only set it if it was unset (after numpy had read it). common.container.paddle_environment now sets one thread in the environment both Paddle workers start with. The language of the searchable PDF is labelled as what it is: the language for placing words (Tesseract's installed packs), not the recognition's.

Standard was tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November.

Choose an engine (the Streamlit page's "legacy engines" expander), built on 27 November 2026, with tests (test_ocr_page.py, with the engines' recognition faked and the rest real, and test_engines.py, test_manual.py in features/ocr/tests/):

  • The form: one drop zone (a PDF, an image, or a ZIP read as a batch, as in Standard), the engines as choices with what each is good at, and the chosen engine's settings: the language (EasyOCR 86, PaddleOCR 106, by name) or what to read (GLM-OCR's three modes); OlmOCR has none. An engine that cannot run is shown switched off with the reason (GLM-OCR without the Ollama server). The button names the engine.
  • The result shows each page beside its text, as in Standard: the lines (PaddleOCR) or blocks (EasyOCR) an engine found are outlined on the page image the engine read, linked to the text; GLM-OCR's tables are shown as tables (sanitized) with a CSV each, and its Markdown rendered; OlmOCR's one Markdown text is shown without a page. A copy button per page. The downloads: Everything (the Streamlit ZIP, now with table CSVs), the text and the engine's JSON. The Streamlit page showed the engines' drawn preview images instead; the web UI does not draw them.
  • A batch gives the result ZIP and an overview: pages, characters and time per file.
  • The engines (features/ocr/engines/): each page keeps the image it was read from and its outlined lines (TextLine); PaddleOCR's worker also returns the straightened page, as PaddleOCR turns and unwarps pages before it finds lines and gives their outlines on that image. Adapters give a description, markdown, ollama_model (so GLM-OCR's model stays loaded when the GPU is released) and problem(). Cancelling: between pages for EasyOCR and GLM-OCR; PaddleOCR's worker and OlmOCR's pipeline are killed at once with the processes they started (run_process gives each a process group; OlmOCR starts vLLM).
  • The service: cancel for recognize_with_engine and recognize_batch_with_engine, which now returns an EngineBatch (the ZIP and the overview; the Streamlit page takes its ZIP), and save_engine_run, which writes the downloads, page images (TIFF and BMP as PNG) and table CSVs and returns the pages to show.
  • Shared with Standard: the pager bar (ocr/macros.html); the markdown filter; nested switches re-apply the switches inside them; the dropzone macro takes an id, for two drop zones on one page.
  • Checked against the image: PaddleOCR 3.3.3 runs its document preprocessor (orientation and UVDoc unwarping) by default, so its outlines belong to doc_preprocessor_res.output_img, which the worker now returns. A smoke run on a GPU node (27 November) read a drawn page with EasyOCR and PaddleOCR through the service and save_engine_run: every outline sits on its text, PaddleOCR's on its straightened page, where the text had moved about 50 px from the original (outlines on the original would have been off by as much). Unwarping also bends a flat page slightly, as on the Streamlit page.
  • The guide's draft: the Choose an engine section of docs/next/ocr.md.

Choose an engine was tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November.

Historic handwriting and Hugging Face model, built on 27 November 2026 as one step (the user's choice), with tests (test_ocr_handwriting_page.py and test_ocr_huggingface_page.py, with the workers faked and the rest real, and in each feature's tests/):

  • Page modules of their own: pages/ocr_handwriting.py and pages/ocr_huggingface.py hold each tool's route and work; the OCR page draws their forms with what their form_context() gives. The switcher's "Soon" mark is gone, as all four tools are built.
  • Historic handwriting: one drop zone (PDF, image or ZIP) and the configured models as choices, each with its description and the models it reads with; the line detector is named. The result shows each page beside its numbered lines, each outlined on the page (<rect>s in the full page's pixels over the page scaled down to 1,600 px) and linked to its text, then the models used, for citation. Downloads: everything with PAGE XML, the text, the JSON with boxes. A batch gives the ZIP and an overview: pages and lines per file.
  • Hugging Face model: one drop zone, the model's name or link, the prompt and the token limit. The user's downloaded models are listed with their size: Use fills the model field, Delete removes one (refused while a Hugging Face job of the session waits or runs). The result shows each page beside the text as the model wrote it (models answer in plain text, Markdown or HTML alike), and the model, revision and prompt. A batch gives the ZIP and an overview: pages and characters per file.
  • The services: cancel for transcribe_document/transcribe_batch and read_document/read_batch (between files and steps; the workers are stopped at once by common.jobs.run_worker); per-file overviews in both BatchRuns; save_transcription and save_run, which write the downloads and page images and return what to show. Handwriting runs now keep the page images, scaled down. The Hugging Face service re-exports the user's model folder (stored_models, delete_model, ...), so the page imports only the service.
  • Shared: common/outputs.py (SavedFile, OutputFolder, web_image), used by the save functions of all three features (the OCR service re-exports SavedFile); uploads.format_names for the drop zones' lists of file types.
  • The guide's draft: the last two sections of docs/next/ocr.md.

Both were tried in the sandbox and committed together on 27 November.

docs.title: Topic Modeling
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, without a mockup (the user asked for the migration straight away), with tests (test_topic_modeling_page.py with the analysis faked, features/topic_modeling/tests/test_overview.py, and the service tests):

  • The collection first: choosing a table or a ZIP of text files uploads it at once; it is read, and its size, columns (the likeliest text column chosen) and first rows come back into the form, with the topics-over-time option (timestamp column, intervals; BERTopic only). The upload waits in a draft job (JobRunner.draft, new); each run copies it into a job of its own, so the same collection can run again with other settings, each run a record of its own (the Streamlit page replaced its result).
  • The form: the algorithms as choices with what each does, the language, each algorithm's settings in a switch (BERTopic's grouping and number of topics in nested switches; its language model, keywords, dimension reduction and outliers folded), and the stability check.
  • The result, drawn in SVG from the run's numbers (the libraries' Plotly and pyLDAvis charts need inline scripts and a CDN, which the web UI does not allow; they stay in the ZIP): the topics beside a map where alike topics lie close (dots and topics linked as OCR's outlines and text), each topic's keywords with weight bars and a few example documents; a similarity heatmap; each topic over time as a small chart to its own peak; the quality scores with what each says. Downloads: everything with the interactive charts, the documents with their topic, the topics with their keywords, and the run's settings and scores.
  • The feature: a new overview.py builds what is drawn the same way for every algorithm, from the keyword weights each engine now keeps and one vector per topic each engine now gives (bertopic_topic_vectors, lda_topic_vectors, top2vec_topic_vectors); classical multidimensional scaling places the topics. TopicModelingResult.overview crosses the worker boundary; summarize_table and save_result serve the page. A failing overview keeps the rest of the run, with a notice.
  • The guide's draft: docs/next/topic_modeling.md.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November (the user liked the look and the options).

Second version of the result (27 November, after the user's review: the three algorithms looked the same, while their libraries draw them differently): each algorithm is now drawn as its own library draws it.

  • LDA, as pyLDAvis: the intertopic distance map (bubbles placed and sized by pyLDAvis, by their share of the words, with its PC axes and size legend) beside the terms: the 30 most salient of the collection until a topic is chosen, then the chosen topic's 30 most relevant, the grey bar a term's overall frequency, the red its frequency in the topic; the lambda slider re-ranks them, and pointing at a term sizes the bubbles by its spread over the topics (app.js). A Documents tab shows each topic's documents with their mixture of topics as a thin bar. The data is pyLDAvis's own, prepared once for its dashboard and for the page (topics in model order, so the numbers match the tables).
  • BERTopic: its keyword score bar charts per topic, the topic map, the documents placed by meaning (UMAP of the embeddings, as visualize_documents; a sample of 1,500), the hierarchy (a dendrogram, average linkage of the topic similarity), the heatmap in the hierarchy's order, and the topics over time on one chart with each interval's words in the tooltips (BERTopic's own topics over time, computed once for its chart and the page).
  • Top2Vec: its word clouds, the topic sizes, the topic map, the documents placed by its document vectors, the heatmap.
  • Emphasis, not a colour per topic (data-viz guidance: categorical colours cap at three for scatter-like charts): grey marks, the topic pointed at or chosen in the accent, the rest faded; one data-region per topic across charts and lists. A muted grey token, --ink-4, for reference marks, checked with the data-viz validator (3:1 on the sheet, apart from the accent with colour-vision deficiency, both themes).
  • Code: features/topic_modeling/overview.py builds the shared parts and each library's (ldavis_parts, the document map, the hierarchy, the words per interval, the clouds, the mixtures); the engines give the inputs (prepare_ldavis, lda_document_topics, topics_over_time_frame, topics_over_time_rows, top2vec_topic_words, document vectors). ui/web/pages/topic_charts.py holds the drawing (TopicsView, moved out of the page module); templates/topic_modeling/view_<algorithm>.html and parts/.
  • Checked with real runs on a CPU node (all three algorithms, a made-up corpus of four themes), rendered with the page's templates and looked at as images: LDA's map, BERTopic's documents, hierarchy, heatmap and over time. Fixed from that look: the size legend moved below the map, bubbles kept clear of the edges, the heatmap sized by its topics.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, without a mockup (the user asked for a modern chat interface in place of Streamlit's), with tests (test_chat_page.py with the model faked; the service's new parts in features/chat/tests/test_service.py):

  • A conversation as modern chat apps show it: the messages on the right in a tinted block (with the files they were sent with), the replies as text, the message box kept at the foot of the window (Enter sends, Shift+Enter starts a new line; it grows with the text), the model chosen beside Send. Streamlit's sidebar became a side panel: the session's conversations, the context meter (with the same notes as before), the downloads, deleting the conversation; on narrow screens it slides in.
  • Several conversations per session (the Streamlit page had one, lost on a reload): kept in the server's memory (app.state.chat) until they are deleted or the session ends; New chat reuses an empty one.
  • Replies are jobs that are not listed (chat/answer.html), as the translation editor's: they wait while another job holds the GPU (and say which, with Cancel that job), and reach the page word by word over the event stream (context.preview(draft, every=0.15)). A reasoning model's thinking shows apart from the answer, folded, with its newest words, and Thought for 12 s when done. Stop stops the model at once (the stream is read in a thread of its own, so even while the model loads) and keeps what was written. Again writes the last answer again, with the model chosen now. Copy gives the answer as Markdown; code blocks have their own.
  • Files: attached with the button or dropped anywhere on the page, up to four, read once (read_document); a file without text is not attached, and the page says why. Tables are kept for the data agents, each in a folder of its own (keep_table; one folder for all would let a second table overwrite the first).
  • The data agents answer data questions as before (the model decides); the reply shows their steps as they work, then the summary, the charts, the statistics and the code. Interactive charts are drawn with plotly.js 3.7.0, vendored as its strict bundle (no unsafe-eval), the version the image's plotly.py writes for; its style rules come from a style sheet read from the bundle (scripts/plotly_css.py), since its own <style> element would be blocked. Visualize Data will use the same.
  • The feature: service.respond replies to a message (pulling the model with progress, routing, the agents or the chat model, stopping); the stream gives the model's thinking apart from its text (Piece); model_options, server_ready, discard_table. The Streamlit page works as before (answer).
  • The job runner: previews can be any object and come more often (every=); page_data holds what a card needs besides the job; the event stream sends the job indicator only when it changed (a reply written word by word changes the runner's version many times a second); a page can name its jobs otherwise than by its id (stream_page), so the stream sends the cards of the conversation shown only, and the page skips cards it has in the same version.
  • The guide's draft: docs/next/chat.md.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November. The user's review asked for two changes, made the same day:

  • The width: the page used the content width of the other pages (78rem), which left the right part of a wide window empty. Chat now takes the whole width beside the index: the conversation in a wider column (60rem) in the middle, the side panel the height of the window against the right edge, as the index is against the left. Below 1280px the panel slides in behind the Conversations button.
  • Following the answer: the page did not keep the answer being written in view. It now follows it with a ResizeObserver on the conversation, whatever changes its size, while a reply is written and for a few seconds after (its charts); scrolling up stops that, and scrolling back to the end or sending a message starts it again. Scroll anchoring is off on the page.

The width was right in the sandbox, the following still not, and the message box stood in the middle of the window with nothing below it. The cause of both: the conversation's element had the class transcript, which the audio player's list of passages already had, with a height limit (28rem) and its own scrolling. The conversation was a box of that height scrolling inside itself: the page could not follow it, and the message box came right after it. It is the thread now, and a test checks that the Chat section of the style sheet shares no class with the rest (test_chat_styles_have_class_names_of_their_own). Before the first message, the welcome stands in the middle of the thread, and the message box at the foot of the window.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November.

docs.title: Visualize Data
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, without a mockup, with tests (test_visualize_data_page.py with the agents faked; the service's new parts in features/visualization/tests/test_service.py):

  • One form, as Topic Modeling's: the table is read as soon as it is chosen, with the agents' own readers, and kept in a draft job while the user writes the request; every analysis links it into a job of its own, so the same table can be asked about again (Streamlit kept one result, lost on a new run or a reload). A new table replaces the one the form names; after a reload the form names none, so the session keeps the newest three tables.
  • The columns come back as a table to tick (Streamlit's column profile and multiselect in one): the type the agents will give each column (number, date, category, or text, from the same rule as their summary, plot_data.column_kind), how full it is, its distinct values and what they are like; All and None, and a count. The first rows are in a second tab. All columns ticked, or none, is the whole table, of which the agents are then told nothing (Streamlit sent every column's name when all were selected).
  • Requests that name the table's columns are suggested under the request box (a distribution, a comparison of groups, the relation of two numbers, an association, a word cloud; example_requests), and What the agents can do replaces Streamlit's capabilities box. The model of the last analysis is offered first.
  • An analysis is a job in the GPU queue. The agents run in the job's thread (service.analyze, new; Streamlit polled a thread of their own), and each of their steps reaches the card as it is taken (the job's preview, shown by a template of the page: preview_template, new in the runner), the newest in view. Cancelling stops them after their current step. A missing model is pulled with its progress, and can be cancelled meanwhile.
  • The result: what was asked, the summary, the statistics (open), the charts with their Python and R code (a chart without R code says why), and the agents' steps folded away; the downloads are the HTML report and the ZIP (service.save_result, which also writes each chart as a file of the job for the page to draw). Charts and statistics are drawn by macros Chat now shares (components/analysis.html), with the styles in a section of their own.
  • Shared: common.model_config.model_options and common.ollama.pull_model (from Chat), render.shorten (from Chat), uploads.copy_into (from Topic Modeling). Every job card carries data-version, and the page skips any card it has in the same version (Chat's rule, now for all pages), so a finished analysis's charts are not drawn again when a new job opens the event stream. Boxes the reader opened stay open on any page (data-keep-open).
  • The rules test now checks every section of the style sheets: a class is styled in one section only.
  • The guide's draft: docs/next/visualize_data.md.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November.

docs.title: Knowledge Graph
docs.text:
Built on 27 November 2026, without a mockup, with tests (test_knowledge_graph_page.py with the reading and the model faked; the feature's new parts in features/knowledge_graph/tests/test_projects.py):

  • Two levels. /knowledge-graph starts a project (an upload or a folder of PDFs on the cluster, counted as its path is typed; a name; where to save it; the model for the topics) or finds saved projects in a folder and opens one. Each project of the session has a page of its own, /knowledge-graph/<id>, with its graph, papers and topics in tabs and its tools (add papers, extract the topics again, rebuild the paper table). Streamlit showed all on one page, one project at a time; the session now keeps every project it opened (app.state.kg_projects), named in links by a random id, never by its path.
  • Builds are jobs: Streamlit ran them in the page, which stayed busy for as long as Grobid and the model worked. A build with the session's model takes the GPU for it; with GPUStack's it needs none. It can be cancelled between papers: the papers read are kept and reused (the card says so: page_data["cancelled"], new). If only the topics fail, the build ends done and says so, as the papers are saved. A missing session model is downloaded first, with its progress. The updates of a project are jobs of its page (knowledge_graph:<id>); a page id <tool>:<key> now links to <tool's path>/<key> in the job indicator and on Home.
  • The graph is drawn by vis-network 9.1.2, vendored as the version Pyvis embeds in the downloads (its dist build adds no <style> element and evaluates no code, so the Content Security Policy needs nothing more), from the nodes, edges and options of draw_graph. Pyvis's own page, which runs inline scripts, stays the download. The options (the view, the node types, the least confidence, the papers shown) draw the graph again at each change; the page keeps the last few views. In the page's type and ink, also in the dark theme; the layout's progress shows while it settles; Fit to view; in the whole collection a click brings out a node's neighbours, as before. The dashed edges the code meant (a topic's category, cited authors) are dashed now: Pyvis passed style, which vis.js does not read. Streamlit also saved each graph page into the project folder; the web UI does not, as the view is downloaded as shown.
  • The feature: build_project, extract_topics_with, read_project, stage_papers (an upload on disk), draw_graph, grobid_problem (a warning before an upload, when Grobid cannot start), gpustack_ready; build_corpus and extract_topics can be stopped between papers, and a stopped or failed topic extraction leaves no partial file. The Streamlit page works as before.
  • With this page every tool is in the web UI.
  • The guide's draft: docs/next/knowledge_graph.md.

Tried in the sandbox and committed on 27 November. Phase 3 is done.

docs.title: Clean-up before the switch
docs.text:
Done on 27 November, before phase 4:

  • Nothing left from the building work: the developer pages under /dev (component gallery, mockups, demo job), TEXT_LAB_WEB_DEV, the placeholder page and the ready flag of the tools with its Soon marks and Home's "under construction" notice are removed, with their styles. The demo job lives on in the tests only (tests/demo_job.py), for the tests of the job runner through the web.
  • Email on start: a box under the job time on the launch form (form.yml), Open OnDemand's bc_email_on_started: Slurm mails the user when the session starts. It goes out with the redeployment of the Open OnDemand files, for both interfaces. The launch guide's draft is docs/next/launch.md.

Next, phase 4: the switch.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Page tests with FastAPI's test client (httpx is in the image), in src/textlab/ui/web/tests/: every route renders, forms refuse bad input, a job runs from submission to download with a fake service, nothing is reachable without logging in, and requests without the CSRF token are refused.
  • Import rules: pages use only the feature services; import-linter already keeps the backend from importing any UI.
  • Manual checks: each page lists in this plan what to try in the sandbox, taken from the features of the Streamlit page it replaces.
  • Browser tests (Playwright) are not planned: the image has no browser.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• The developer guide and the feature READMEs change with each page's commit, as usual.
  • The user guide describes what production runs. Each new page's guide is written with the page under docs/next/, which the published site leaves out (exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml), and replaces the current guide at the switch.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation The browser opens at most 6 connections to the proxy at a time (HTTP/1.1), for all its tabs on the site together One event stream per page, open only while jobs are active; one upload at a time Features are lost on the way A checklist per page, from the Streamlit page; the switch waits for every page New widgets are needed: editable tables (OCR review, Topic Modeling), charts, streamed chat, the graph view, the audio player HTML tables with inputs, or a vendored grid library; plotly.js vendored; SSE; pyvis output in a frame; the player's own JavaScript ported Most services cannot be cancelled yet Added with each page Features change in the Streamlit pages during the migration Streamlit pages get bug fixes only

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The command-line and batch tools (cli.py, deploy/sbatch/) stay placeholders.
  • More than one user per server: each Open OnDemand session keeps its own app.
  • Translating the interface: English only, as now.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: None at the moment. Decided on 27 November: survey extraction (the experimental check box of automatic OCR, with its review of the detected form) is left out of the new UI; the survey feature stays in the backend for now.
